content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I'm new to this field and need step-by-step instructions for connecting a PT100 temperature sensor to a [product_name] expansion module ([product_name] AM2 PT100) and viewing the measurement on the [product_name] operator panel. Currently, I have a [product_name] base module and an AM2 PT100 expansion. Thanks in advance for any help!
Hi, please consult the product documentation for the AM2 PT100, where you'll find the necessary wiring diagram.
In addition to the manual and product information included with the PT100 module, you can also refer to this FAQ: [url]

Once you've connected the PT100 following the manual, you can test it using a cup of hot coffee and a glass of cold water. Create a small [product_name] program with an analog input linked to an analog amplifier, ending with an analog flag. Add a message text block and connect it to an open connector. Enable the message text by setting its input to be always active. In the analog amplifier block, choose PT100 as your sensor type; gain and offset will be auto-set to -500 and 2000. Set display resolution to 0.1 Celsius and one decimal place for accurate readings. In the message text block, activate the latest features for the relevant [version_no] family. Add text like 'Temp.' and insert the corresponding amplified analog value. Above the window, use the bar graph icon to display the temperature range—tap water is about 10°C, coffee about 80°C. Set the graph bar to about 12 characters on the third line and label the fourth line with '10' and '80' at each end. You can also add the degree C symbol. A tip: changing the character set in message text settings (under file menu) to GBK or SJIS allows 16 characters per line, except for special symbols. This helps create more informative displays. Simulate, download, run—play with it and enjoy!
Thanks everyone, you really helped me out. Much appreciated!
